attempted_claim: Consider the focusing cubic wave equation in R^{1+6}: ∂_t^2 u − Δu − u^3 = 0, (t,x) in I×R^6, with radial data (u_0,u_1) in Ḣ^2×Ḣ^1(R^6) (scaling-critical regularity s_c=2, energy-supercritical). Let u⃗(t) be the radial strong solution with maximal interval I_max=(T_−,T_+)∋0. Prove: if sup_{t in [0,T_+)} ‖u⃗(t)‖_{Ḣ^2×Ḣ^1(R^6)} < ∞, then T_+=+∞ and u⃗(t) scatters to a free wave as t→+∞; in particular any radial finite-time blow-up solution satisfies limsup_{t→T_+} ‖u⃗(t)‖_{Ḣ^2×Ḣ^1(R^6)} = ∞.
decisive_failure: The Kenig-Merle rigidity steps (critical stability, profile decomposition, critical element, Hdot^2 channel-of-energy and Liouville/cascade exclusion) were mapped but not proved; numerical ODE heuristics are suggestive only and were not elevated to claims. No complete proof or independently valuable finding was established.
